objectives: To systematically synthesise the published evidence on the feasibility, acceptability, and effectiveness of digitally delivered multimodal prehabilitation interventions for cancer patients; specifically, to evaluate feasibility and acceptability, assess effects on patient outcomes such as physical fitness, psychological readiness, nutritional status, and quality of life, and explore patient and provider perspectives on using these interventions in cancer care.
inclusion_criteria: Primary quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-methods studies of digitally delivered multimodal prehabilitation for cancer patients. Eligible participants were adults aged 18 years or older with a cancer diagnosis and/or healthcare professionals involved in cancer care. Interventions had to focus on the prehabilitation phase before primary treatment (for example surgery, chemotherapy, or radiotherapy), include all three components of multimodal prehabilitation (physical, nutritional, and psychological), and be delivered digitally (for example via wearable fitness trackers, telehealth platforms, or mobile health applications). Outcomes of interest included feasibility, acceptability, physical fitness, psychological readiness, nutritional status, and quality of life. Searches were limited to peer-reviewed English-language studies published from January 2008 onward.
exclusion_criteria: Conference abstracts, editorials, commentaries, protocols, and reviews were excluded. Studies were also excluded if they did not involve adult cancer patients or relevant healthcare professionals, were not focused on the pre-treatment prehabilitation period, were not digitally delivered, or were not multimodal across physical, nutritional, and psychological domains. The PRISMA full-text exclusions were: not multimodal (n=8), duplicate record (n=4), not intervention study (n=4), not digitally delivered (n=2), protocol only (n=2), and developmental/usability study (n=1).
